**Status:** skeleton. The questions and the data are fixed; the analysis is not
written yet, so nothing below is a result.

This post replaces `posts/logistic-separation/`, which was deleted outright
rather than moved. That URL now returns 404 and inbound links to it are broken
on purpose.

## The two questions

"Is Nigeria getting worse?" is a national average doing all the talking. The
claim worth testing is that the country holds at least two trajectories, and
that the states worsening fastest are not the states that are already worst.
If that holds, the headline number is not a summary of the country — it is a
summary of Borno.

The second question is not really one question. Frequency and lethality are
different conflicts: a month can be the deadliest in the country without being
the most violent, and which month you name depends on whether danger means the
observed maximum, the probability of being worst, or the risk of crossing a
catastrophe threshold. Those three definitions will disagree on real data, and
the disagreement is the finding.

## The data

A balanced state-LGA-month panel, 1997 to mid-2026, built from the Kaggle
Nigerian insecurity dataset (ACLED and UCDP via HDX, MIT licence). The grain is
one row per `(state, lga, year, month)`; 765 distinct LGA names cover 772 cells
because seven names repeat across states, so the pair is the key and the name
alone is not.

Most rows record no events at all. That is a modelling fact rather than a data
problem, and it is why the count models below are the obvious starting point
and the zero-inflation question is a real one.

The file carries no actors, event types, exact dates, coordinates or population.
Two consequences, stated now rather than discovered later: "banditry versus
Boko Haram" is not answerable from it, and "worse" will mean per area, not per
capita, unless a population table is joined in.

Fit on 2015–2025, hold 2026 out entirely and score against it. 2026 is six
months, not a missing half-year.

## The method

A hierarchical negative binomial with state-varying slopes — partial pooling,
so a small state's trend is pulled toward the national one and a large state's
is left alone. Structure chosen by AIC across nested specifications; the
predictive claim scored by CRPS on the held-out 2026.

Gradient boosting runs alongside as a control, scored on the same hold-out with
the same leakage discipline. It is there to be beaten on evidence, not to be
included for its own sake: on a few dozen states the capacity has nothing to
learn from.

## Still to write

The trend estimates and their intervals, the three competing definitions of
"worse" side by side, the per-LGA deadliest months, the seasonality split
between event counts and death counts, and every caveat that belongs in the
post rather than in a footnote.
